
---
title: "Why LLMs in healthcare?"
---

::: {.callout-note}
### Key Takeaways

- LLMs excel at **language tasks**: summarising, drafting, translating, extracting, and answering questions with citations.
- Use **retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG)** to ground outputs in trusted local guidelines, pathways, and formularies.
- Apply **human‑in‑the‑loop** review for all clinical outputs; LLMs can be helpful but are fallible.
- Prioritise **data privacy, governance, and prompt hygiene** when handling sensitive information.
:::


### Administrative Tasks


- **AI Scribes (LLM-powered)**: Convert ambient consultation audio into structured draft notes (history, exam, plan) and generate draft discharge summaries or clinic letters. This can save 5-10 minutes per patient appointment.
  
- **Summarisation & Standardisation**: Turn lengthy free-text notes into succinct summaries; convert variable discharge letters into standard templates with required fields; translate patient correspondence into plain language or other languages.

- **Information Extraction**: Pull key entities (medications, allergies, dates, diagnoses) from unstructured clinical text for registry updates, handover lists, or quality improvement audits.



### Clinical Decision Support

- **Guideline Q&A with Citations (RAG)**: Ask questions against trusted sources (local pathways, formulary, NICE/BNF, institutional policies) and receive grounded answers with direct links to source passages.

- **Chart Summarisation & Timeline Reconstruction**: Condense years of notes into problem-oriented summaries; surface relevant history, medication changes, and key investigations to aid clinical decision-making during reviews or handovers.

- **Differential & Plan Drafting (for review)**: Generate candidate differential diagnoses, red flags, and draft management plans **that must be checked** by the clinician against current guidelines and individual patient context.


::: {.callout-important}
## Human-in-the-Loop Principle
All LLM-generated clinical documentation must be **reviewed, verified, and signed** by the responsible clinician. You remain professionally and legally accountable for clinical records. Human review is essential to mitigate hallucinations, misinterpretations, and negligence risks.
:::

### Research and Innovation: Accelerating Evidence Work

- **Literature Triage & Summarisation**: Screen abstracts against inclusion criteria; create structured summaries (PICO framework) from papers; accelerate systematic review processes.

- **Protocol & Document Drafting**: Produce first drafts of study protocols, ethics applications.


### Operational Efficiency: Improving Service Delivery

- **Policy & SOP Q&A (RAG)**: Enable staff to query institutional policies, safeguarding procedures, and escalation pathways.

- **Patient Education Materials**: Generate patient-specific educational leaflets and discharge instructions in accessible language.
